site.name: Lucky Strike / Last Nickel Mine
site.location: Dry Lake / Grand Island mining district
overview: Lucky Strike and Last Nickel are documented together as a Boulder County mine locality in federal mineral records, associated with tungsten and lead-zinc mineralization near Dry Lake.

A 1952 Defense Minerals Administration docket grouped Lucky Strike, Last Nickel, and Silver King under applicant Fred E. Pelton in the Grand Island area, while later U.S. Geological Survey mineral-resource data preserves Lucky Strike and Last Nickel as the same mapped Dry Lake locality.

timeline.text: Defense Minerals Administration docket 0158 recorded Lucky Strike, Last Nickel, and Silver King together in Boulder County for tungsten and lead-zinc exploration; the application was denied.
U.S. Geological Survey Mineral Resources Data System records retained Lucky Strike (Last Nickel) as a named Dry Lake mineral locality in Boulder County.

moreHistory: Federal exploration-assistance records identify the property group in Township 1 South, Range 72 West, Section 1, 6th Principal Meridian, within the Grand Island area of Boulder County.

The federal docket documents tungsten and lead-zinc as the principal commodities associated with the grouped property. Later mineral-resource locality data treats Lucky Strike and Last Nickel as one Dry Lake locality, supporting their combined identity here while Silver King remains a separate name in the 1952 property grouping.

The mapped locality point at approximately 39.966667, -105.458333 is used as a site-level identification point. It represents a historic mineral locality, not a field survey of a surviving shaft or portal.
